newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses turn bullish again,led by London.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses turn bullish again,led by London.

text.p: European stocks turned bullish again on Tuesday, making healthy gains at the close with London climbing nearly one percent on the back of a strong showing by oil companies.

In currency markets, the dollar ended up a pfennig after the Bundesbank on Tuesday kept its key repo rate steady at 3.00 percent although many traders took the view that the threat of rising German rates remained in the market.

The big advance on European bourses contrasted with Monday's dull showing when investors were badly rattled by a sharp Wall Street fall on Friday, leading to fears that the recent bull run was petering out.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, led the way on Tuesday. Shrugging off a stronger-than-forecast British inflation figure for July, the blue-chip FTSE 100 index closed up 43.9 points at 5075.8, within a whisker of its closing record.
The rally, fed by a favourable outlook for UK interest rates , saw sharp gains in oil company shares, including British Petroleum Plc, retailers, led by Kingfisher Plc, and supermarkets.

The FTSE 250,the broad-based index loaded with Britain's biggest manufacturers, finished 28.8 points higher at 4,700.4, near its record 4,736.2. The all-share index rose 18.87 points to an all-time best close of 2,376.39.
The FTSE 250 has gained about four percent since last Thursday, when the Bank of England hiked interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent.

Investors have switched into the currency-sensitive stocks, which had been hit by fears that strong sterling was biting into their earnings, after the Bank signalled that interest rates were on hold for now, traders said.

Paris, which ended down on Monday, had a volatile morning. After shedding most of its early gains, the bourse recovered to end up half a percentage point, supported by the stronger dollar, traders said.

Business picked up late in the afternoon after the market had drifted lower, with interest focusing on companies due to report first-half sales this week. Wall Street, which made an unsettled start, offered little direction.

In Frankfurt, floor trade stocks closed up 0.7 percent and after-hours deals on the computerised IBIS index surged by over one percent in late transactions but volumes left the market vulnerable to important U.S. data due on Wednesday.
"This is summer lull stuff," said a Munich trader. "People are a bit wary of some really crucial reports due in the U.S."
Data to be released in the U.S. on Wednesday includes retail sales and producer prices, both key indicators of inflation trends in the influential American economy.
The currency markets were firmly focused on the Bundesbank with traders digesting the effect of the "no-change" rate move.
The dollar staged a minor rally after on the Bundesbank's announcement but it failed to build up monetum during the session and ended the day at 1.8665 marks, up about a pfennig on Monday's close.

Traders are likely to keep speculating about German rates ahead of the Bundesbank council meeting August 21. "After next week's council meeting the probability of a move should rise again," said Kay Sinden, economist at Bankers Trust.
Sinden said the effective easing of monetary conditions because of the mark's weaknesss and its inflationary implications were likely to make the case for higher German rates more convincing.

The British pound, which initially moved in sympathy with the dollar, fell against the U.S. currency and the mark near the close after remarks by a government official that British inflation would drop soon, discouraging talk of higher interest rates.

Sterling fell by over a cent to $1.5775 and by half a pfennig to 2.9430 as Junior Treasury minister Geoffrey Robinson said underlying inflation would drop back to the government's 2.5 percent target in the next couple of months.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8665 marks and 116.12 yen, compared with 1.8543 and 115.78 in late trading on Monday
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 43.9 points at 5,075.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 29.96 points at 4,363.09 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index finished 15.13 points at 2,998.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was closed a $326.35 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $327.25. Silver was down a cent at $4.42 in late trade.
